title: MAGIC-Based High-Speed Adders for in-Memory Computing Using Memristors
problem: In-memory computing with memristive crossbar arrays using MAGIC and IMPLY logic requires efficient arithmetic circuits. Existing MAGIC-based RCA designs are slow, requiring many computational steps.
motivation: Optimized memristor-based adders exploiting parallel processing across crossbar rows/columns can reduce step count and improve throughput for in-memory arithmetic operations.
method: Semi-serial full adder design using MAGIC logic (10 computational steps in 3x7 crossbar). Two RCA designs optimizing parallelism: one using semi-serial full adder, another using serial full adder. Both achieve 2x speedup vs. existing MAGIC RCA designs.
key_novelty: Optimized memristor-based RCA designs using MAGIC logic with parallel row/column processing achieving 2x speedup through improved dataflow and reduced step counts.
contributions: Semi-serial full adder in MAGIC logic (10 steps)
Serial full adder variant: 199 steps for 32-bit RCA
Semi-serial full adder variant: 232 steps for 32-bit RCA
2x speedup vs. previous MAGIC RCA designs
limitations: Abstract only; no comparison with IMPLY logic or conventional computing; total latency in physical time units not provided; no energy efficiency analysis; limited to 32-bit demonstration.
